title: USDC from Any Chain to Your L1
summary: CCIP to the C-Chain, then ICTT to your L1
description: One transaction on Base, Ethereum, Arbitrum or OP moves USDC to your Avalanche L1: CCIP carries it to a gateway on the C-Chain, which forwards it through your ICTT bridge in the same execution. If the L1 leg cannot run, the gateway holds the USDC for a retry or a refund instead of losing it.
prompts: Let users bring USDC from Base straight to my L1
Onboard stablecoins from any chain into my Avalanche L1
One-click USDC top-up from Ethereum to my L1's gas token

Deploying the sender on the source chain is signed by the builder's wallet

checks.description: The recipient holds the USDC on the L1 (ERC20TokenRemote bridges)

review: The gateway checks the (source selector, sender) allowlist in _ccipReceive and in getCCVsAndFinalityConfig, and accepts exactly one token: the hub's USDC.
A failed ICTT leg never reverts the CCIP execution: the transfer is held, anyone can retry it, and the recipient or owner can refund it on the C-Chain.
Each CCIP message id is processed once; the gateway rejects duplicates.
gatewayGasLimit in extraArgs covers the forwarding (measured about 307,000); too little makes the whole CCIP execution fail and need a manual retry.
The recipient controls the same address on the C-Chain, which is where a refund goes if the L1 leg keeps failing.

frontend.summary: Deposit USDC from another chain straight onto the L1 in one transaction, and see it land in the L1 wallet.
audience: Users arriving with USDC on Base, Ethereum or another chain who want to use the L1
Support staff helping someone whose deposit was held
journeys: Deposit: pick the source chain, enter an amount against the balance there, and see the fee and the L1 address it lands in (their own by default).
Follow one timeline: sent on the source chain, crossing to Avalanche, forwarded to the L1, arrived, with a wait estimate at each stage.
Recover a held deposit in plain words ('Your USDC is safe on Avalanche. Try again, or get it back on the C-Chain.') with Retry and Refund buttons.
Finish on the L1 balance, the thing they came for, with a link into the L1 app.
flows: On the source chain: encode extraArgs with the gateway gas limit, quote getFee, approve USDC for the sender, then sendToL1(recipient, amount, 0x0, extraArgs) with the fee as value.
Track the CCIP message on https://ccip.chain.link, then watch ForwardedToL1 or ForwardHeld on the gateway for that message id.
On a held transfer, offer Retry (anyone) and Refund on the C-Chain (recipient).
Show the L1 balance of the recipient; for a NativeTokenRemote bridge that is the native balance.
